entries.question: What visa will I arrive on, and how does it convert to residency?
entries.answer:
Most newcomers arrive either on a work entry permit (issued by their employer) or a visit/tourist visa. For
employment routes, your employer or sponsoring company applies for a residence entry permit tied to your job offer.
Once you enter the UAE on that permit, your status is changed to residency, followed by medical fitness, Emirates ID
biometrics, and issuance of the residence permit. For visit/tourist arrivals, you typically cannot convert directly to
residency without an approved sponsor and visa application; instead, your sponsor files a residence visa application
and you either change status inside the UAE or exit and re-enter on the entry permit, depending on the route.

sources.text:
UAE Government Visa & Emirates ID – General provisions for residence visa: https://u.ae/en/information-
and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/residence-visa
ICP – Issuing Residency Permit service: https://smartservices.icp.gov.ae

entries.question: Can my wife come on my sponsorship, and what documents does she need?
entries.answer:
Yes, if you hold a valid UAE residence visa and meet the minimum salary and housing requirements, you can
sponsor your spouse. Typical documents include: your passport and residence visa, your employment contract or
salary certificate, attested marriage certificate, passport copies and photos of your spouse, housing lease contract
(Ejari/Tawtheeq), and medical insurance as required. The attested marriage certificate is critical—without it, spousal
sponsorship is usually not accepted.

entries.question: Do our marriage and education certificates need attestation, and where?
entries.answer:
Yes. Marriage certificates almost always need to be attested in the country of issue, then by the UAE
embassy/consulate there, and finally by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFAIC) on arrival. Education
certificates (especially for skilled roles or professional licensing) often require similar attestation if they are used for
visa category, professional classification, or licensing. The exact requirements depend on your visa type and emirate,
but as a safe rule: assume marriage and key education certificates must be fully attested before you rely on them for
residency or employment.

entries.question: Do the children's birth certificates need attestation?
entries.answer:
Yes, if you plan to use your children’s birth certificates for residency sponsorship, school enrolment, or
official records, they should be attested in the country of issue, then by the UAE embassy/consulate, and finally by
MoFAIC in the UAE. For newborns in the UAE, the local birth certificate is issued here and then attested locally as
needed.

sources.text:
UAE Government – Residence visa documents (children): https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-
emirates-id/residence-visa
MoFAIC – Attestation of foreign birth certificates: https://www.mofa.gov.ae

entries.question: What is the medical fitness test, where do I do it, and how long does it take?
entries.answer:
The medical fitness test is mandatory for all new residents. It includes a blood test and chest X-ray to screen
for communicable diseases. In Abu Dhabi, you complete it at SEHA Visa Screening Centers. The process usually takes
15–30 minutes, and results are typically issued within 24–48 hours. You cannot receive your residence visa or
Emirates ID until this step is completed.

sources.text:
UAE Government – Residency medical test: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-
id/residence-visa (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: How do I apply for an Emirates ID, and how long until I get it?
entries.answer:
Your Emirates ID application is submitted automatically when your employer or sponsor files your residency
visa. After your medical fitness test, you will receive an SMS to complete biometrics at an ICP service center. The
Emirates ID card is usually issued within 5–10 working days after biometrics, though timelines vary.

sources.text: ICP – Emirates ID Services: https://smartservices.icp.gov.ae (smartservices.icp.gov.ae in Bing)

UAE Government – Emirates ID: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/emirates-id
(u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: What is TAMM and do I need an account?
entries.answer:
TAMM is Abu Dhabi’s unified government services platform. It centralizes services such as residency,
housing, licensing, utilities, and more. You will need a TAMM account to access many Abu Dhabi-specific services,
especially once your Emirates ID is active.

entries.question: What is UAE Pass and why do I need it?
entries.answer:
UAE Pass is the national digital identity used to log into almost all government portals, including TAMM, ICP,
and healthcare systems. It allows secure authentication, digital signatures, and access to official documents. You
should set it up within your first week.

entries.question: How do I get my wife's residency processed once mine is done?
entries.answer:
Once your residency is issued, you can apply to sponsor your wife through ICP or TAMM. Steps include: entry
permit, medical fitness test, Emirates ID application, and visa stamping. You must meet salary and housing
requirements and provide an attested marriage certificate.

sources.text:
Sponsoring family members: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/residence-
visa/sponsoring-family-members (u.ae in Bing)
ICP Smart Services: https://smartservices.icp.gov.ae (smartservices.icp.gov.ae in Bing)

entries.question: What happens if my Emirates ID is delayed — can I still rent, bank, enrol children?
entries.answer:
If your Emirates ID is delayed, you can still complete most tasks using your residency visa stamp or Emirates
ID application receipt.
• Renting: Allowed with visa stamp + passport.
• Banking: Some banks accept the application receipt.
• School enrolment: Schools accept passport + visa. Delays are common and rarely block essential steps.

sources.text: ICP – Emirates ID application tracking: https://smartservices.icp.gov.ae (smartservices.icp.gov.ae in Bing)

entries.question: Who do I contact if my employer is slow processing my visa?
entries.answer:
If your employer delays your visa processing beyond reasonable timelines, you can contact MoHRE to file a
complaint or request clarification. You can also check your visa status directly through ICP. Employers are legally
required to process visas promptly.

sources.text: ICP Visa Status: https://smartservices.icp.gov.ae (smartservices.icp.gov.ae in Bing)

entries.question: How do I register with my embassy?
entries.answer:
Most embassies encourage residents to register for consular support. You can register online through your
embassy’s website or visit the embassy in Abu Dhabi. Registration helps with:
• Emergency contact
• Passport renewal
• Voting (if applicable)
• Consular assistance
Check your home country’s embassy website for the exact process.

sources.text:
Directory of foreign embassies in UAE: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/justice-and-
safety/embassies-and-consulates-in-the-uae

entries.question: Should we book temporary accommodation first, and for how long?
entries.answer:
Yes. Most families book temporary accommodation (hotel, serviced apartment, or Airbnb-style stay) for 2–4
weeks to allow time for: completing medical fitness, Emirates ID biometrics, viewing properties, and signing a
tenancy contract. Booking too short a stay can create pressure if residency or housing steps are delayed; booking
around 3 weeks is a practical balance for most newcomers.

sources.text: Launch in Dubai – Residency timelines & medical/ID sequence: https://launchindubai.com
Abu Dhabi housing and tenancy guidance: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/housing

entries.question: Which areas suit families, and roughly what does rent cost?
entries.answer:
Popular family-friendly areas in Abu Dhabi include Khalifa City A, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Reef,
Saadiyat Island, Al Raha Gardens, and Al Reem Island. Typical annual rents (approximate):
• 1BR: AED 55,000–90,000
• 2BR: AED 75,000–130,000
• 3BR: AED 110,000–180,000+ Prices vary by building age, amenities, and proximity to schools.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Housing Info: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/housing (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: How many cheques is rent usually paid in?
entries.answer:
Rent in Abu Dhabi is typically paid in 1–4 cheques per year.
• 1 cheque often gives the best price.
• 2–4 cheques offer flexibility but may slightly increase the rent. Some landlords now accept monthly
payments via direct debit or digital platforms.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi tenancy guidance: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/housing (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: What is Tawtheeq and who registers it?
entries.answer:
Tawtheeq is Abu Dhabi’s official tenancy registration system. It validates your rental contract and is required
for:
• Sponsoring family members
• School enrolment
• Utility setup
• Residency processes
The landlord or real estate agent usually registers Tawtheeq, but tenants can request updates or corrections through
TAMM.

entries.question: What deposit and agent fees should I expect?
entries.answer:
Typical costs include:
• Security deposit: 5% of annual rent (unfurnished) or 10% (furnished)
• Agent commission: Usually 2–5% of annual rent or a fixed fee
• Contract typing / admin fees: AED 100–300 These vary by landlord and agency.

entries.question: Can I rent before I have residency?
entries.answer:
Yes. Many landlords allow renting with a passport + entry permit. However, to register Tawtheeq, you will
eventually need your residency visa. You can sign the contract before residency, but full activation of utilities and
some services may require your Emirates ID or visa stamp.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi tenancy rules: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/housing (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: How do I set up water and electricity (ADDC)?
entries.answer:
Water and electricity in Abu Dhabi are provided by ADDC (Abu Dhabi Distribution Company). To activate
service, you need:
• Tawtheeq contract
• Emirates ID or residency visa
• Passport copy
Activation is usually completed within 24–48 hours.

entries.question: How do I get internet installed, and how long does it take?
entries.answer:
Internet is provided by Etisalat or du. You will need:
• Passport + visa or Emirates ID
• Tawtheeq contract
• Address details
Installation typically takes 1–3 days, depending on building access and technician availability.

entries.question: What should I check in a tenancy contract before signing?
entries.answer:
Key items to review:
• Rent amount and number of cheques
• Maintenance responsibilities
• Notice period
• Renewal terms
• Deposit amount
• Included amenities (parking, chiller, facilities)
• Penalties for early termination
• Accuracy of unit details (size, location, furnishings)
Always ensure the contract matches what was agreed verbally.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi tenancy guidelines: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/housing (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: How do I find and compare schools?
entries.answer:
School selection in Abu Dhabi is centralized through ADEK (Abu Dhabi Department of Education and
Knowledge). Their official portal provides school ratings, curriculum details, fees, inspection reports, and contact
information. You can filter by curriculum, location, grade level, and performance. Private school comparison platforms
(e.g., Edarabia) offer additional parent reviews.

entries.question: What curricula are available, and how do they compare to ours?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi offers multiple international curricula:
• British (UK)
• American (US)
• IB (International Baccalaureate)
• Indian (CBSE/ICSE)
• French
• Canadian
• UAE Ministry of Education curriculum
British, American, and IB are the most common among expat families. ADEK provides detailed inspection reports
explaining academic standards, teaching quality, and curriculum alignment.

entries.question: What documents are needed for school enrolment?
entries.answer:
Most schools require:
• Child’s passport + residence visa
• Birth certificate (attested if issued abroad)
• Vaccination records
• Previous school reports/transcripts
• Transfer certificate (attested if required)
• Emirates ID (or application receipt) Requirements vary slightly by curriculum and grade level.

sources.text: UAE Government – Education Services: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/education (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: When does the school year start, and can children join mid-year?
entries.answer:
Most Abu Dhabi schools begin the academic year in late August or early September. Yes, children can join
mid-year depending on seat availability. Schools often accept mid-year transfers, especially for expat families arriving
after the term begins.

sources.text: School-specific calendars (various): Search “Abu Dhabi school calendar”

entries.question: What are typical fees, and does my employer contribute?
entries.answer:
Annual school fees vary widely:
• Nursery: AED 20,000–50,000
• Primary: AED 30,000–60,000
• Secondary: AED 40,000–90,000+
Some employers offer education allowances, especially for senior roles or government-linked entities. Check your
employment contract for details.

entries.question: Is there a school bus, and how do I arrange it?
entries.answer:
Most schools offer bus services through approved transport providers. You register directly with the school
during enrolment. Bus routes, fees, and pickup/drop-off schedules vary by school and location. ADEK regulates safety
standards for school transport.

entries.question: What’s the process if my child needs learning support?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi schools must comply with inclusive education policies. If your child needs learning support,
schools typically offer:
• Individual learning plans (ILPs)
• Special education needs (SEN) coordinators
• Additional support classes
• External assessments (if required)
ADEK mandates that schools provide reasonable accommodations and cannot refuse admission solely based on
learning needs.

sources.text: UAE Government – Inclusive Education: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/education (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: What vaccinations or medical records should we bring?
entries.answer:
You should bring full vaccination records for all family members, especially children, as schools and nurseries
often require proof of immunisation (e.g., MMR, polio, DTP). For adults, bring records of chronic conditions,
prescriptions, and any specialist reports. While the UAE does not usually require vaccination proof for residency itself,
having complete records simplifies school enrolment, continuity of care, and insurance approvals.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Department of Health (DoH): https://www.doh.gov.ae
Sample expat medical guidance – Launch in Dubai (Emirates ID & medical): https://launchindubai.com

entries.question: Is health insurance mandatory, and who provides it for my wife and children?
entries.answer:
Yes — health insurance is mandatory for all Abu Dhabi residents. Under Abu Dhabi law, employers must
provide health insurance for employees, but dependents (wife and children) are usually the responsibility of the
sponsoring resident. Some employers offer dependent coverage, but this is not guaranteed.
You must ensure your family has valid insurance before residency is fully activated. Insurance is typically arranged
through approved providers such as Daman, ADNIC, or private insurers.

sources.text: DoH Abu Dhabi – Health Insurance Requirements: https://www.doh.gov.ae

UAE Government – Health Insurance: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/health-and-fitness/health-
insurance (u.ae in Bing) (bing.com in Bing)

entries.question: How do I register with a doctor or clinic?
entries.answer:
You do not “register” with a doctor in the UAE the way some countries require. Instead, once you have
health insurance, you can visit any clinic or hospital within your insurance network. Your insurer’s app or website will
show:
• Network hospitals
• Network clinics
• Co-pay amounts
• Approval requirements
For chronic conditions, you may need referral letters depending on your insurance plan.

sources.text: DoH Abu Dhabi – Healthcare Facilities: https://www.doh.gov.ae

entries.question: Where do I go in an emergency?
entries.answer:
In Abu Dhabi, emergency care is available at major hospitals such as Sheikh Shakhbout Medical City (SSMC),
Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, Burjeel Hospital, and Mediclinic branches. Dial 999 for police/emergency response and
998 for ambulance services. Emergency treatment is provided regardless of insurance status, but follow-up care may
require approval.

sources.text:
Abu Dhabi Emergency Services: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/justice-and-safety/emergency-
numbers (u.ae in Bing) (bing.com in Bing)

entries.question: Can I get my regular prescription medication here?
entries.answer:
Most common prescription medications are available in Abu Dhabi. Bring your existing prescriptions and
doctor’s reports, especially for controlled medications. Some medicines are classified as controlled substances and
require:
• A local doctor’s consultation
• A UAE prescription
• Possible approval from the Ministry of Health
Always check whether your medication is allowed before arrival.

sources.text: DoH Abu Dhabi – Pharmacy Services: https://www.doh.gov.ae

entries.question: Is my wife's maternity care covered?
entries.answer:
Maternity coverage depends on your insurance plan. Most Abu Dhabi insurance policies include:
• Prenatal checkups
• Scans
• Delivery (normal or C-section)
• Postnatal care
However, coverage limits vary widely. Some plans require a waiting period (often 6–12 months) before maternity
benefits activate. Always confirm coverage details with your insurer.

sources.text: DoH Abu Dhabi – Maternity Services: https://www.doh.gov.ae

entries.question: Can we ship household goods, and what's restricted?
entries.answer:
Yes, you can ship household goods to Abu Dhabi using international movers. Standard household items are
generally allowed, but restricted or prohibited items include: weapons, certain chemicals, counterfeit goods, and
materials that violate local cultural or religious norms. Some electronics or communications equipment may require
approval. Your mover will usually provide a customs compliance list, and you should check UAE customs regulations
before shipping.

entries.question: Can we bring our pet?
entries.answer:
Yes, many families bring pets to Abu Dhabi, but you must comply with UAE pet import rules. This typically
includes: microchipping, valid vaccinations (especially rabies), health certificate, and sometimes serology tests, plus
an import permit issued by the UAE authorities. Certain breeds may be restricted. Airlines also have their own rules
for pet transport, so you must coordinate both UAE import regulations and airline policies.

sources.text: UAE Ministry of Climate Change & Environment – Pet import: https://www.moccae.gov.ae
Abu Dhabi Municipality – Veterinary & pet regulations: https://www.abudhabi.ae

entries.question: What's the best time of year to arrive?
entries.answer:
From a comfort and logistics perspective, many families prefer arriving between
October and March, when temperatures are milder and the school year is in progress. Arriving just before the school
year (August/September) can also make sense if you’re focused on enrolment, but it’s hotter and more intense. There
is no “official best time,” but avoiding peak summer heat and aligning with school and work cycles usually makes the
transition smoother.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi tourism & climate information: https://visitabudhabi.ae
School calendars (various Abu Dhabi schools): https://adek.gov.ae

entries.question: How do I get a local SIM card?
entries.answer:
You can purchase a SIM card from Etisalat or du at airports, malls, or service centers. You must present your
passport and entry permit or residency visa. Tourist SIMs are available immediately; resident SIMs require Emirates
ID or the application receipt.

entries.question: Can I drive on my home licence, and for how long?
entries.answer:
If you hold a licence from an approved country (e.g., UK, US, Canada, EU, Australia, New Zealand, South
Africa), you may drive in the UAE temporarily on your home licence until your residency visa is issued. Once you
become a resident, you must convert your licence to a UAE licence. Tourists can drive on their home licence +
international driving permit.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Police – Driving Licence Services: https://www.adpolice.gov.ae

UAE Government – Driving in the UAE: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/transport/driving-in-the-
uae

entries.question: How do I convert my driving licence?
entries.answer:
Residents from approved countries can convert their licence without a driving test. You will need:
• Emirates ID
• Passport + visa
• Original home-country licence
• Eye test
• Fee payment
Conversion is done through TAMM or Abu Dhabi Police service centers. Residents from non-approved countries must
take driving lessons and pass the UAE driving test.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Police – Licence Services: https://www.adpolice.gov.ae

entries.question: How do I buy or lease a car, and what insurance is needed?
entries.answer:
You can buy a car through dealerships (new or certified used) or private sellers. Leasing is available through
major rental companies (e.g., Hertz, Thrifty, Dollar). To register a car, you need:
• Emirates ID
• Valid UAE driving licence
• Insurance policy
• Vehicle inspection (for used cars)
Insurance is mandatory. Options include:
• Third-party liability (minimum legal requirement)
• Comprehensive insurance (recommended for new or financed cars)

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Police – Vehicle Registration: https://www.adpolice.gov.ae

entries.question: Is public transport practical for daily use?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi’s public transport system includes buses, taxis, and ride-hailing apps. Buses are reliable and
affordable, but coverage varies by area — excellent in central Abu Dhabi, limited in outer suburbs. Many families rely
on cars for daily commuting due to heat and distance. Taxis and apps (Careem, Uber) are widely available.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Integrated Transport Centre (ITC): https://itc.gov.ae

entries.question: How do I get a Hafilat card or use taxis and ride apps?
entries.answer:
The Hafilat card is Abu Dhabi’s bus payment card. You can purchase and top it up at:
• Bus stations
• Ticket vending machines
• ITC customer centers
Taxis can be booked via:
• TransAD dispatch
• Careem
• Uber
• Street pickup
Ride-hailing apps require a UAE mobile number and valid payment method.

entries.question: What laws or customs should we be aware of that differ from home?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi is welcoming and multicultural, but there are important laws and customs to respect:
• Public behavior: Avoid public displays of affection; respect modesty norms.
• Alcohol: Only permitted in licensed venues; drunk driving is zero-tolerance.
• Photography: Avoid photographing government buildings or people without consent.
• Dress code: Modest clothing recommended in public places.
• Respect for religion: Avoid loud behavior near mosques; Friday is a holy day.
• Drugs: Zero-tolerance; penalties are severe.
These norms ensure smooth integration and avoid legal issues.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Tourism – Cultural guidance: https://visitabudhabi.ae

entries.question: What should we expect during Ramadan?
entries.answer:
During Ramadan:
• Working hours are reduced.
• Many restaurants remain open but may have screened dining areas.
• Eating, drinking, or smoking in public during daylight hours is discouraged.
• The city becomes more social in the evenings, with Iftar and Suhoor gatherings.
• Malls and restaurants stay open later.
Ramadan is a peaceful, family-oriented period and newcomers often enjoy the cultural experience.

sources.text: Visit Abu Dhabi – Ramadan in the UAE: https://visitabudhabi.ae

entries.question: Where can we find community groups, places of worship, or newcomer networks?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi offers diverse community hubs:
• Places of worship: Mosques, churches, temples (Hindu temple in Abu Dhabi), Sikh gurdwaras.
• Community groups: Expat clubs, cultural associations, sports groups.
• Newcomer networks: Internations, Meetup groups, Facebook expat communities.
• Cultural centers: Manarat Al Saadiyat, Qasr Al Hosn, Louvre Abu Dhabi events.
These spaces help families integrate socially and culturally.

sources.text:
Places of Worship Directory (UAE Government): https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/justice-and-
safety/places-of-worship
Visit Abu Dhabi – Community & Culture: https://visitabudhabi.ae

entries.question: How do I register a home address officially?
entries.answer:
Your home address in Abu Dhabi is officially registered through your Tawtheeq tenancy contract. Once
Tawtheeq is issued, your address is automatically linked to your Emirates ID and appears in government systems such
as TAMM, ICP, and MoHRE. If you move, your landlord or agent must update Tawtheeq, which updates your address
across government platforms.

sources.text: UAE Government – Housing Services: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/housing (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: How do I get a PO Box or receive mail?
entries.answer:
The UAE does not deliver mail directly to homes. You must either:
• Rent a PO Box from Emirates Post, or
• Use a MyHome service (delivery to your building), or
• Receive packages via courier companies (Aramex, DHL, FedEx)
PO Boxes can be rented online and activated immediately.

sources.text: Emirates Post – PO Box Services: https://www.emiratespost.ae

UAE Government – Postal Services: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/transport/postal-services (u.ae
in Bing)

entries.question: What are typical utility bills per month?
entries.answer:
Utility bills vary by apartment size and usage:
• 1BR: AED 200–350/month
• 2BR: AED 300–500/month
• 3BR: AED 450–700/month If your building has district cooling, you may pay an additional AED 300–
600/month depending on provider and usage.

entries.question: Where do I shop for groceries, and what will cost more than at home?
entries.answer:
Popular grocery stores include Carrefour, Lulu, Spinneys, Waitrose, and Coop. Imported goods (cheese,
berries, specialty items) are more expensive, while local produce, poultry, and staples are reasonably priced. Online
grocery delivery is widely available via Careem, Instashop, and Carrefour Online.

entries.question: Are alcohol and pork available, and what are the rules?
entries.answer:
Yes — alcohol and pork are available in licensed stores and restaurants. Rules:
• Alcohol purchase requires no special permit in Abu Dhabi.
• Consumption is allowed in licensed venues and private homes.
• Drunk driving is strictly zero-tolerance.
• Pork is sold in designated sections of major supermarkets.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Tourism – Dining & Nightlife: https://visitabudhabi.ae

UAE Government – Social Etiquette & Laws: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/justice-and-
safety/social-etiquette-and-laws-in-the-uae (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: How do I dispose of bulky waste or recycle?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi Municipality provides free bulky waste collection. You can request pickup through TAMM.
Recycling bins are available in many communities for paper, plastic, and glass. Some areas also have dedicated
recycling centers.

entries.question: What apps does everyone here use (delivery, government, transport)?
entries.answer:
Common apps include:
• Government: UAE Pass, TAMM, ICP Smart Services
• Transport: Careem, Uber, Hafilat, Abu Dhabi Taxi
• Delivery: Talabat, Deliveroo, Careem Food
• Groceries: Instashop, Carrefour Online
• Utilities: ADDC, Etisalat, du
These apps make daily life significantly easier.

entries.question: Can I get domestic help, and how is a housemaid visa sponsored?
entries.answer:
Yes — domestic workers can be hired through:
• Tadbeer centers (government-approved)
• Licensed agencies
• Direct sponsorship (if eligible)
To sponsor a maid directly, you must meet salary requirements and provide accommodation. The process includes:
• Entry permit
• Medical fitness test
• Emirates ID
• Visa stamping
Tadbeer offers full-service packages including recruitment, visas, and training.

sources.text:
UAE Government – Domestic Worker Rules: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/jobs/domestic-
workers (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: Can my wife work on my sponsorship?
entries.answer:
Yes. She can work while sponsored by you, but she must obtain a work permit from the Ministry of Human
Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE). The employer issues the permit; she does not need a separate employment
visa.

entries.question: How does my wife meet people if she isn't working?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi has many ways for spouses to build social networks:
• Community groups (Facebook, Meetup, Internations)
• Fitness classes, yoga studios, and sports clubs
• Volunteering opportunities
• Parent groups at schools and nurseries
• Cultural centers and workshops
• Expat women’s networks (e.g., Abu Dhabi Moms, Women’s Circle)
Social life is active and newcomers integrate quickly.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Community Groups (Visit Abu Dhabi): https://visitabudhabi.ae

entries.question: Can my wife open her own bank account?
entries.answer:
Yes — once she has her residence visa and Emirates ID (or the Emirates ID application receipt), she can open
her own bank account. Most banks allow dependents to open:
• Savings accounts
• Current accounts
• Credit cards (subject to income requirements)
She does not need to be employed to open a basic account.

entries.question: Can my wife study or take courses here?
entries.answer:
Yes — she can enroll in:
• Universities
• Training institutes
• Professional certification programs
• Language schools
• Online courses with UAE accreditation
Most institutions accept dependent visas. Some professional programs may require additional documentation.

entries.question: Can my wife sponsor a family member to visit?
entries.answer:
Yes — if she holds a valid UAE residence visa, she can sponsor visit visas for:
• Parents
• Siblings
• Other relatives (depending on category)
Requirements include:
• Proof of relationship
• Financial capability
• Valid Emirates ID
• Passport copies of the visitor

entries.question: How do we get a visit visa for my parents?
entries.answer:
You can apply through ICP Smart Services or TAMM. Required documents:
• Your Emirates ID
• Your passport + visa
• Parents’ passport copies
• Proof of relationship (birth certificate)
• Financial proof (salary certificate or bank statement)
Visit visas are typically issued for 30, 60, or 90 days, with extension options.

entries.question: Can my parents live with us long-term?
entries.answer:
Yes — but only under specific residency categories. Options include:
• Family residency sponsorship (salary requirements apply)
• Long-term visit visas
• Golden Visa (if they qualify through investment or special categories)
Parent sponsorship requires higher salary thresholds and proof of dependency.

entries.question: What childcare or nursery options exist for under-fours?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi has many nurseries offering:
• British EYFS curriculum
• Montessori programs
• Play-based learning
• Bilingual Arabic-English options
Nurseries are regulated by ADEK, which provides inspection reports and licensing information.

entries.question: What happens if we have a baby here — birth certificate, visa, passport?
entries.answer:
If your baby is born in Abu Dhabi:
1. Birth notification is issued by the hospital.
2. You apply for the birth certificate through TAMM.
3. You get the certificate attested by MoFAIC.
4. Apply for your baby’s passport through your embassy.
5. Apply for your baby’s residence visa through ICP.
You must complete residency procedures within 120 days of birth.

entries.question: Is there paternity leave?
entries.answer:
Yes — UAE Labour Law grants 5 days of paid paternity leave for private-sector employees. Leave can be
taken within 6 months of the child’s birth.

entries.question: How much cash or savings should we have for the first two months?
entries.answer:
For a family, a practical rule of thumb is to have 2–3 months of living costs
available in cash or easily accessible savings. This typically covers: rent and deposit, school application fees,
transport, groceries, basic furniture, and unexpected admin costs. In Abu Dhabi, many families budget AED 20,000–
40,000 for initial setup, depending on housing choice and school fees. This is not a legal requirement, but a practical
planning figure based on typical expat costs.

sources.text: BusinessDubai – UAE residence visa chain & costs: https://businessdubai.ae
Abu Dhabi cost-of-living and housing guides (various): https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/housing

entries.question: Can I open a bank account before my Emirates ID arrives?
entries.answer:
Most banks require at least the Emirates ID application receipt or residency visa stamp to open an account.
A few banks allow “non-resident accounts” or “salary transfer accounts” with passport + entry permit, but full
accounts typically require Emirates ID. Always check with the bank directly.

sources.text:
UAE Government – Banking for residents: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/finance-and-investment
(u.ae in Bing)
Bank-specific onboarding pages (ADCB, FAB, Emirates NBD)

entries.question: How do I get my salary paid — what is WPS?
entries.answer:
In Abu Dhabi, salaries are paid through the Wage Protection System (WPS), a government-mandated payroll
system that ensures employees receive their salaries on time and in full. Your employer must:
• Register you in WPS
• Transfer your salary through an approved bank or exchange house
• Follow UAE labour regulations for payment timing
You simply provide your bank account details once your account is opened.

sources.text:
UAE Government – WPS Overview: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/jobs/wage-protection-system
(u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: What do I need to open a bank account, and which banks are newcomer-friendly?
entries.answer:
To open a resident bank account, you typically need:
• Passport + residence visa
• Emirates ID (or application receipt)
• Salary certificate or employment contract
• Proof of address (Tawtheeq or tenancy contract)
Newcomer-friendly banks include ADCB, FAB, Emirates NBD, Mashreq, and HSBC, all of which have expat onboarding
processes.

sources.text:
UAE Government – Banking Services: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/finance-and-investment (u.ae
in Bing)
Bank onboarding pages (ADCB, FAB, Emirates NBD)

entries.question: Can I get a credit card in the first year?
entries.answer:
Yes — most banks issue credit cards to new residents once you have:
• A salary account
• A minimum monthly income (often AED 5,000–10,000 depending on the card)
• A stable employment contract
Some banks may require 3 months of salary history, but many issue cards immediately for eligible salary brackets.

sources.text:
UAE Government – Banking & Credit: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/finance-and-investment
(u.ae in Bing)
Bank credit card eligibility pages (varies by bank)

entries.question: How do I transfer money home cheaply?
entries.answer:
You can transfer money using:
• Bank transfers (convenient but sometimes higher fees)
• Exchange houses (Al Ansari, Lulu Exchange, UAE Exchange)
• Online remittance apps (Wise, Remitly, Western Union digital)
Exchange houses and digital apps often offer the best rates and lowest fees.

sources.text:
UAE Government – Financial Services: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/finance-and-investment
(u.ae in Bing)
Major exchange houses (Al Ansari, Lulu Exchange)

entries.question: Is there income tax, and what about tax obligations back home?
entries.answer:
The UAE does not impose personal income tax on salaries. However, you may still have tax obligations in
your home country, depending on:
• Residency rules
• Worldwide income laws
• Double taxation agreements
Always check with a tax advisor familiar with your home country’s regulations.

entries.question: What is end-of-service gratuity and how is it calculated?
entries.answer:
End-of-service gratuity is a lump-sum payment given when you leave your job. Calculation:
• 21 days of basic salary per year for the first 5 years
• 30 days of basic salary per year after 5 years It is based on basic salary, not total compensation.

sources.text: UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021)

entries.question: Do I need a will here, and what happens to my assets if I die in the UAE?
entries.answer:
It is strongly recommended for expats to have a UAE-registered will, especially if you have family and assets
in the country. Without a will, local courts may distribute assets according to UAE personal status laws, which may
differ from your home country’s inheritance rules. You can register a will through:
• ADJD (Abu Dhabi Judicial Department)
• DIFC Wills Service Centre (Dubai, but valid for Abu Dhabi assets)

entries.question: How do I budget for annual costs like school fees, rent cheques and insurance?
entries.answer:
Annual budgeting in Abu Dhabi typically includes:
• Rent (1–4 cheques per year)
• School fees (termly or annually)
• Health insurance (annual)
• Car insurance & registration
• Utility bills
• Travel
• Groceries & transport
Many families use budgeting apps or simple spreadsheets to plan for large annual payments.

sources.text: UAE Government – Cost of Living: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/housing (u.ae in Bing)

entries.question: What should be in my employment contract before I sign?
entries.answer:
Your UAE employment contract should clearly state:
• Job title and description
• Basic salary + allowances
• Working hours
• Leave entitlements
• Probation period
• Notice period
• Health insurance coverage
• End-of-service benefits
• WPS salary payment details
• Any additional benefits (housing, schooling, flights)
Contracts must comply with UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021) and be registered with MoHRE.

entries.question: What is the probation period and can I leave during it?
entries.answer:
Probation periods in the UAE are typically 3–6 months. You can resign during probation, but you must give:
• 14 days’ notice if leaving the UAE
• 30 days’ notice if transferring to another UAE employer
Your employer can also terminate employment during probation with 14 days’ notice.

entries.question: What is a labour ban, and does it still apply?
entries.answer:
Labour bans were common under older labour laws but are now rare. Under current regulations, bans
generally apply only if:
• You violate your contract
• You abscond
• You breach labour regulations
Most employees can change jobs freely as long as notice periods and contractual obligations are met.

entries.question: Can I do freelance or side work on an employment visa?
entries.answer:
Yes — but only with the correct work permit. You cannot legally freelance or take side jobs without a
part-time work permit or freelance permit issued by MoHRE or a free zone. Working without a permit can result in
fines for both you and the employer.

entries.question: What are the rules for changing employers?
entries.answer:
You can change employers if you:
• Complete your notice period
• Have your current employer cancel your visa
• Sign a new employment contract
• Obtain a new work permit
No-objection certificates (NOCs) are not required under current labour law. Your new employer handles the visa
transfer through MoHRE and ICP.

entries.question: What is a golden visa and could I qualify later?
entries.answer:
The Golden Visa is a long-term residency (5 or 10 years) for eligible categories such as:
• Investors
• Entrepreneurs
• Highly skilled professionals
• Outstanding students
• Specialized talent (medicine, science, culture)
Eligibility depends on income, qualifications, investment, or professional achievements. Many expats qualify later in
their career.

sources.text: ICP – Golden Visa Services: https://smartservices.icp.gov.ae (smartservices.icp.gov.ae in Bing)

entries.question: What happens to my family's residency if I lose my job?
entries.answer:
If your employment ends, your residence visa is typically cancelled within 30 days. Your dependents’ visas are
tied to yours, so they must also be cancelled or transferred. You have a grace period (usually 30–180 days depending
on visa type) to:
• Find a new job
• Transfer your visa
• Apply for a different residency category
Your family can remain legally during the grace period.

sources.text: ICP – Visa Cancellation & Grace Periods: https://smartservices.icp.gov.ae (smartservices.icp.gov.ae in Bing)

entries.question: How do I file a complaint against my employer?
entries.answer:
You can file a labour complaint through MoHRE via:
• The MoHRE app
• The MoHRE website
• The call center (600 590000)
• A Tasheel service center
MoHRE will mediate between you and your employer. If unresolved, the case may be escalated to the labour courts.

entries.question: What are the emergency numbers?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi has simple, unified emergency numbers:
• 999 — Police & general emergencies
• 998 — Ambulance
• 997 — Fire
• 996 — Coast Guard
• 991 — Electricity emergencies (ADDC)
Emergency services are fast, reliable, and available 24/7.

entries.question: How safe is it to walk at night or leave things in the car?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi is consistently ranked among the safest cities in the world.
• Walking at night is generally safe in most neighborhoods.
• Petty theft is rare, but you should still avoid leaving valuables visible in cars.
• Police presence is strong and response times are fast.
Safety is one of the biggest advantages for families living in the UAE.

sources.text: Numbeo Safety Index (Abu Dhabi ranked #1 globally multiple years): https://www.numbeo.com/crime

entries.question: What do I do if I lose my passport or Emirates ID?
entries.answer:
If you lose your passport:
1. Report the loss to Abu Dhabi Police.
2. Obtain a police report.
3. Visit your embassy to apply for a replacement or emergency passport.
If you lose your Emirates ID:
1. Report the loss through ICP Smart Services.
2. Apply for a replacement card.
3. Provide your passport and residency details.
Lost Emirates IDs are common and easily replaced.

sources.text: ICP – Emirates ID Replacement: https://smartservices.icp.gov.ae (smartservices.icp.gov.ae in Bing)

UAE Government – Lost Passport Procedures: https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/justice-and-
safety/lost-and-found

entries.question: What happens if I get a traffic fine or my car is impounded?
entries.answer:
Traffic fines must be paid through:
• TAMM
• Abu Dhabi Police app
• Police service centers
If your car is impounded (e.g., major speeding, dangerous driving), you must:
• Pay the fine
• Complete any required courses
• Wait for the impound period to finish (varies by violation)
Abu Dhabi has strict road safety laws, especially for speeding.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Police – Traffic Violations: https://www.adpolice.gov.ae

entries.question: How do I report a dispute with a landlord?
entries.answer:
Landlord–tenant disputes in Abu Dhabi are handled by the Rent Dispute Settlement Committee. Steps:
1. Attempt resolution with the landlord.
2. File a case through TAMM.
3. Provide tenancy contract, Tawtheeq, receipts, and evidence.
4. Attend hearings if required.
The committee issues legally binding decisions.

entries.question: What are the penalties for bounced cheques?
entries.answer:
Bounced cheques are taken seriously in the UAE. Penalties may include:
• Fines
• Bank account restrictions
• Civil claims
• In some cases, criminal charges (depending on amount and intent)
Many banks now offer direct debit or online payments to reduce cheque reliance.

entries.question: When can we buy property, and where can foreigners buy?
entries.answer:
Foreigners with any valid UAE residency (employment, family, investor, Golden Visa) can buy property in
designated freehold areas. In Abu Dhabi, expats can buy in:
• Al Reem Island
• Yas Island
• Saadiyat Island
• Al Raha Beach
• Masdar City
• Al Maryah Island
You can buy apartments, villas, and townhouses. Ownership is typically freehold or 99-year leasehold, depending on
the development.

sources.text: DARI Abu Dhabi (official real estate portal): https://www.dari.ae

entries.question: Can I get a mortgage as a resident?
entries.answer:
Yes — residents can apply for mortgages through UAE banks. Typical requirements:
• Minimum salary (often AED 10,000–15,000)
• Stable employment
• Good credit history
• Down payment: 20% for expats (minimum by law)
Mortgage terms usually range from 15–25 years. Golden Visa holders may receive more flexible terms.

sources.text: UAE Central Bank – Mortgage Regulations: https://www.centralbank.ae
Major banks (FAB, ADCB, HSBC) mortgage pages

entries.question: How do I bring my own business or start one here?
entries.answer:
You can start a business in Abu Dhabi through:
• Mainland licensing (via Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development – ADDED)
• Free zones (e.g., ADGM, Hub71, TwoFour54, Masdar City)
Steps include:
1. Choose business activity
2. Apply for trade licence
3. Register with relevant authorities
4. Obtain visas for yourself and employees
Free zones offer 100% foreign ownership and simplified setup.

entries.question: How do I get a UAE driving licence that works internationally?
entries.answer:
Once you have a UAE driving licence, you can apply for an International Driving Permit (IDP) through:
• Automobile & Touring Club of the UAE (ATCUAE)
• Select service centers and online portals
The IDP allows you to drive in most countries worldwide.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Police – Licence Services: https://www.adpolice.gov.ae

entries.question: Can I apply for citizenship or permanent residency eventually?
entries.answer:
UAE citizenship is rare and granted only under exceptional circumstances (e.g., special contributions,
long-term service, or nomination by UAE leadership). Permanent residency is available through the Golden Visa,
which offers 5–10 year renewable residency for eligible categories such as investors, professionals, and outstanding
talent.

entries.question: What pension or retirement options exist for expats?
entries.answer:
Expats do not receive UAE government pensions. Retirement planning typically includes:
• Employer savings schemes
• Private investment plans
• Offshore retirement accounts
• End-of-service gratuity (mandatory)
Some employers offer Employee Savings Plans (ESPs) similar to pension schemes.

entries.question: How do we plan for children's university — local or abroad?
entries.answer:
Abu Dhabi has strong universities (NYU Abu Dhabi, Khalifa University, Sorbonne Abu Dhabi). Many expat
families also send children abroad. Planning typically includes:
• Saving early (education plans, investment accounts)
• Checking scholarship options
• Reviewing university entry requirements
• Ensuring curriculum alignment (IB, A-Levels, AP, CBSE)

entries.question: What do I need to cancel when we leave — visa, Tawtheeq, utilities, bank?
entries.answer:
When leaving Abu Dhabi permanently, you must cancel or close several services:
Residency & Government
• Cancel your residence visa through your employer or ICP.
• Cancel dependents’ visas.
Housing
• Close your Tawtheeq tenancy contract.
• Settle final ADDC (water/electricity) bills.
• Cancel internet (Etisalat/du).
Financial
• Close your bank accounts (optional but recommended).
• Cancel credit cards.
• Settle any outstanding loans.
Other
• Cancel insurance policies.
• Return company assets (if applicable).

entries.question: Can I ship goods out and take my car?
entries.answer:
Yes — you can ship household goods internationally using movers. To export your car, you must:
• Clear any fines
• Cancel registration
• Obtain export plates
• Complete customs clearance
• Arrange shipping with a certified exporter
Some countries require additional inspections or compliance checks.

sources.text: Abu Dhabi Police – Vehicle Export: https://www.adpolice.gov.ae

entries.question: How do I get my gratuity and deposits back?
entries.answer:
End-of-service gratuity is paid by your employer after visa cancellation. You must:
• Complete exit formalities
• Return company property
• Ensure WPS salary records are up to date
Housing deposits are refunded after:
• Final inspection
• Settlement of utility bills
• Contract closure (Tawtheeq)
Refund timelines vary by landlord.

entries.question: What records should I keep after leaving?
entries.answer:
Keep copies of:
• Final salary & gratuity statements
• Visa cancellation certificates
• Tawtheeq cancellation
• Utility clearance certificates
• Tax records (if applicable)
• Employment references
• Insurance closure documents
These documents help with future employment, immigration, or financial processes.

entries.question: What if we want to come back later?
entries.answer:
You can return to Abu Dhabi anytime on:
• A new employment visa
• A family sponsorship visa
• A Golden Visa (if eligible)
• A visit visa
Past residency does not restrict future entry. If you left with no fines or violations, re-entry is straightforward.
